requirement: Describe PALMS-II as a prospective single-center mixed-methods pilot with a qualitative adaptation phase followed by a two-arm randomized feasibility phase in community-residing adults with multiple sclerosis.

evidence.text: The proposal states the primary development and pilot-testing objective and defines Phase 1 qualitative interviews and Phase 2 randomized feasibility testing.

requirement: Keep the Phase 1 qualitative convenience sample of five adults distinct from the Phase 2 randomized efficacy and feasibility population; do not pool their observations into one treatment-effect analysis.

evidence.text: Phase 1 uses individual qualitative interviews with five adults, whereas Phase 2 is a randomized controlled pilot of 20 adults.

requirement: Define the Phase 2 intervention as eight weekly 90-minute remotely delivered group MAPSS-MS cognitive self-management sessions emphasizing physical activity, and the comparator as enhanced usual care consisting of an illustrated physical-activity booklet.

evidence.text: The intervention group receives eight weekly 90-minute web-based group sessions, while control receives the NCHPAD physical-activity booklet.

requirement: Preserve the Phase 2 1:1 randomized allocation target of 10 participants per arm and the blinded collection of NIH Toolbox outcomes by a trained research assistant.

evidence.text: The protocol assigns 20 Phase 2 participants as 10 intervention and 10 control and states that a research assistant blinded to group assignment collects NIH Toolbox measures.

requirement: Before finalization, specify sequence generation, allocation concealment, implementation roles and any stratification or blocking; do not invent these details from the word randomized.

evidence.text: The protocol says participants will be randomly assigned 10 per arm but gives no operational randomization procedure.

requirement: State the prospective targets of five Phase 1 participants and 20 Phase 2 participants, 10 per randomized arm, and label the study as a pilot without a supplied power calculation; do not replace the target with registry actual enrollment.

evidence.text: The proposal prospectively targets five interview participants and 20 randomized pilot participants but provides no effect-size or power derivation.

requirement: Define baseline and eight-week post-intervention as the two Phase 2 assessment times, with post-intervention collection within two weeks after the final class for intervention participants and 8-10 weeks after baseline for controls.
acceptable_values: within two weeks after final class

evidence.text: Phase 2 data are collected at baseline and eight weeks, with arm-specific operational timing for the post-intervention visit.

requirement: Before finalization, identify the governing primary outcome or explicitly declare the pilot analyses exploratory, reconciling the broad development/feasibility objective with the many cognitive, physical-activity, sleep and self-management measures rather than silently selecting one.

evidence.text: The protocol states a development and feasibility objective and enumerates many outcome measures without a single statistical primary hierarchy.

requirement: Operationalize the eight NIH Toolbox cognitive tests and prespecify whether they are analyzed individually, by domain or as a validated composite, including score type, direction, baseline-to-eight-week derivation and treatment contrast.
acceptable_values: individual domain or validated composite rule

evidence.text: The protocol lists eight NIH Toolbox tests spanning language, executive function, attention, working memory, processing speed and episodic memory without an analysis-level aggregation rule.

requirement: Cover the prespecified patient-reported domains separately: MS self-management, self-efficacy for medications/treatments, symptoms and daily activities, perceived cognitive function, depression, fatigue and sleep disturbance.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies MSSM-R and the PROMIS and Neuro-QoL short forms for the named patient-reported domains.

requirement: Define ActiGraph derivations for steps, activity counts, total sleep time, wake after sleep onset, sleep efficiency, sleep latency and awakenings, including valid wear-day/night criteria and participant-level aggregation across seven days and nights.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies wrist accelerometry for seven days and nights and names physical-activity and sleep variables but not valid-wear or aggregation algorithms.

requirement: For Phase 1 interviews, apply the prespecified Miles and Huberman content-analysis workflow with independent initial transcript review, team review and finalized themes concerning content, sessions and participation barriers.
acceptable_values: initial review by PI and second team member

evidence.text: The qualitative analysis section specifies Miles and Huberman content analysis, initial review by two team members and team finalization of themes.

requirement: If the reference ANCOVA is retained, specify the outcome-by-outcome model, treatment term, baseline outcome adjustment, effect estimate and confidence interval, and prospectively justify any additional continuous covariates such as age or time since diagnosis.

evidence.text: The reference plan says ANCOVA will compare groups while controlling continuous variables such as age and length of diagnosis, but does not define endpoint-specific models or baseline adjustment.

requirement: Define the randomized analysis population and retain attribution by assigned arm, with explicit rules for no intervention attendance, partial session attendance, control crossover, use of outside cognitive or exercise programs and absence of any post-baseline assessment.

evidence.text: The protocol defines randomized arms and eight intervention sessions but no analysis population or treatment-attribution rules.

requirement: Prespecify item-level scoring and participant-level missing-data rules for questionnaires, NIH Toolbox and ActiGraph outcomes, a primary missingness assumption and sensitivity analysis; do not treat unobserved eight-week outcomes as zero change.

evidence.text: The protocol schedules multiple instruments and seven-day wearable measurement but neither document supplies missing-data rules.

requirement: Define a confirmatory outcome family and multiplicity procedure, or explicitly label the many cognitive, self-management, symptom, activity and sleep comparisons exploratory and avoid claiming efficacy from isolated p-values.

evidence.text: Many correlated outcomes are collected across multiple domains, while the protocol and reference plan define no hierarchy or multiplicity control.

requirement: If the reference pilot threshold of alpha less than 0.10 is used, state whether it is one- or two-sided, align confidence intervals to that choice and distinguish exploratory signals from confirmatory success.

evidence.text: The reference plan specifies alpha <0.10 but does not state sidedness, confidence intervals or a success family.

requirement: Report internal-consistency reliability for each applicable multi-item instrument and use the reference criterion greater than 0.70, while keeping reliability distinct from between-arm intervention effects.

evidence.text: The reference plan calls for internal-consistency estimates for each instrument and treats alphas >0.70 as acceptable.

requirement: Operationalize feasibility outcomes with numerators, denominators, assessment windows and any benchmarks for recruitment, retention, session delivery, videoconferencing problems and solutions, completion of outcome measurement and seven-day ActiGraph wearability.

evidence.text: Aim 2 identifies recruitment, delivery and measurement as process outcomes.
The reference plan says feasibility trends include recruitment, retention, web-platform problems and ActiGraph wearability but gives no denominators or thresholds.

requirement: Address the two intervention delivery cohorts of four to six participants by specifying whether cohort clustering or session-level effects are modeled, adjusted with small-sample methods or treated as a design limitation.

evidence.text: The 10 intervention participants are divided into two remotely delivered cohorts of four to six, but no cohort-effect analysis is specified.

requirement: Provide descriptive summaries of demographic and illness-related baseline variables by randomized arm and overall, without using baseline significance testing as an allocation-balance gate.

evidence.text: The reference plan calls for descriptive analysis of demographic and illness-related sample characteristics.

requirement: Define safety collection and summary for falls or trips, transient worsening of MS symptoms and distress related to cognitive testing, including the Phase 2 safety population, observation window, severity, relatedness, serious events and arm-level incidence.

evidence.text: The safety-monitoring section names likely physical and distress events and continuous review but supplies no statistical safety conventions.
